body:
Re: Existence is a bubble

meredith@shadow.net (William R. Meredith) writes:
> The man ... did not do a great deal of TV watching or interacting
> with others for that matter. Hell he never even got lay in his life.

Right, I just take this as TK lashing out again at a culture that he
views as doing him wrong.  I take away from TK's writing that he
was saying, "Maybe I wouldn't be so dang unhappy if there were more
thoughtful and introspective people around me and less of the
"manipulated masses".  This is his TV complaint -- It's cluttered
the world with humans that he views as less valuable.  TK would
like *quality* human lives, not quantity.  And who will decide what
quality is?  TK.  This is not sounding so good.  

FC writes in paragraph 147...
> Entertainment provides modern man with an essential means of escape.
> While absorbed in television, videos, etc., he can forget stress,
> anxiety, frustration, dissatisfaction. Many primitive peoples, when
> they don't have work to do, are quite content to sit for hours at a
> time doing nothing at all, because they are at peace with
> themselves and their world. But most modern people must be
> constantly occupied or entertained, otherwise they get "bored,"
> i.e., they get fidgety, uneasy, irritable.

It's OK to have strong ideas like this and express them in writing,
but to force them on others by killing people is another.  It's all
a values call, and TK's values are far from the norm.

> He is a complete misfit, who only sense of power came from killing
> others!

Well, I'm neither TK nor a psychologist so I can't speak on how he
felt about his bombings, but I could believe that this is the case.

E
